title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten documented KU spaces for quiet work, group projects, creative production, research, and campus connection.

cards.title: Watson Library
cards.subtitle: 1425 Jayhawk Blvd. • library study hub
cards.notes: Start on the third floor for group tables, computers, FitDesks, carrels, and Studio K; move upstairs when your task needs a quieter setting.
cards.short_summary: A central library building with distinct study setups across three upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Watson as a location with group and quiet study areas, computer workstations, scanners, printers, and reservable study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Check KU Libraries’ current hours before going; study rooms support academic study and research.

cards.entity_name: Watson Library Fifth Floor Study Space
cards.title: Watson’s Fifth-Floor Study Space
cards.subtitle: Watson Library • quiet individual work
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from low noise; the fifth floor combines quiet individual study with International Collections and a reflection room.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet-study floor inside Watson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries lists quiet individual study space, International Collections, and a reflection room on Watson Library’s fifth floor.
cards.access_notes: Conversation and phone use are not permitted in Watson’s designated quiet-study areas, including the fifth floor.

cards.title: Studio K
cards.subtitle: Watson Library third floor • quick recording studio
cards.notes: Use this named room when a class presentation or demonstration needs recording; reserve it with the video equipment purpose in mind.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in recording studio for speeches, demonstrations, and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries describes Studio K as a quick-record studio where users can record a speech, demonstration, or presentation shortly after arriving.
cards.access_notes: Priority use goes to KU students, staff, or faculty using the room’s video-recording equipment.

cards.title: Anschutz Library
cards.subtitle: KU Libraries • study, support, and technology
cards.notes: Choose Anschutz for a project needing research help, writing support, tutoring, or computer access; check the floor map before meeting a group.
cards.short_summary: A library building that concentrates academic support, technology, and varied study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says Anschutz hosts research, writing, and technology help, tutoring, collaboration spaces, and study areas.
cards.access_notes: Open computer areas on the third and fourth floors contain more than 100 workstations.

cards.title: David Beaham Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library fourth floor • quiet study
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need a named quiet room for solo reading or writing; keep the space suited to focused, low-noise work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room in Anschutz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies the David Beaham Reading Room as a quiet study room on the east portion of Anschutz Library’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Quiet areas are set aside for reading, solo computer work, and other quiet tasks.

cards.title: Anschutz Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library second floor • creative work
cards.notes: Reserve time for a hands-on project, podcasting, or 3D-printing exploration; beginners and curious makers are explicitly welcomed by KU Libraries.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor creative space for making, recording, and collaborative experimentation.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries describes the Anschutz Makerspace as a second-floor space with tools for 3D printing, podcasting, and creative discovery.
cards.access_notes: The floor map lists the Makerspace on Anschutz Library’s second floor; confirm reservation procedures with KU Libraries.

cards.title: Anschutz Reflection Room
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library third floor • reflection space
cards.notes: Use this separate room for quiet reflection or prayer, respecting people of all faiths, spiritual beliefs, and practices while you share the space.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor space for peaceful reflection within Anschutz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries’ floor map lists a Reflection Room on the third floor of Anschutz Library.
cards.access_notes: KU Libraries asks users of reflection spaces to practice tolerance of all faiths, spiritual beliefs, and practices.

cards.title: Spahr Engineering Library
cards.subtitle: LEEP2 • individual and collaborative study
cards.notes: Use Spahr for engineering-focused work with collaborators, then reserve a group room through your KU email or Engineering Student Success if needed.
cards.short_summary: An engineering-library setting with individual, collaborative, and group-study options.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says Spahr Engineering Library includes individual and collaborative study spaces, group study rooms, and desktop workstations.
cards.access_notes: Desktop computer access is limited to KU School of Engineering affiliates; group rooms can be reserved through KU email or Engineering Student Success.

cards.title: Murphy Art & Architecture Library
cards.subtitle: Spencer Museum of Art, Level 1 • research library
cards.notes: Pair a museum-area visit with on-site research in this named library; use the collections there when art, design, architecture, or planning work needs sources.
cards.short_summary: An art and architecture research library located in the Spencer Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Murphy Art & Architecture Library in the Spencer Museum of Art and states it is open to any on-site user.
cards.access_notes: The library is open to on-site users; borrowing privileges and use rules vary by material.

cards.title: Marilyn Stokstad Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Kenneth Spencer Research Library • primary-source research
cards.notes: Create an Aeon account and request materials before working with special collections; check in at the third-floor reception desk when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections reading room for working with Spencer Research Library materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenneth Spencer Research Library provides research services in the Marilyn Stokstad Reading Room and requires an Aeon account for on-site collection access.
cards.source_title: Use Collections | Kenneth Spencer Research Library
cards.access_notes: No appointment is necessary to use collections, but researchers must have a current Aeon account and follow Reading Room policies.
